I'm interest in getting my first road racing bike, I've always had mountain bikes previously, and hoping to get a little advice.

I'm interested in a [Claud Butler Limoix](http://www.jejamescycles.co.uk/claud-butler-limoux-road-bike-id89108.html). I'm struggling to find any review about that particularly bike. Can anyone give any opinions? As far as I can tell about Claud Butler, they seem an *okay* brand, but they're not your Specialized or Cannondale. This is a nice price compared to a Allez or CAAD 8.

I like this one because, the price, disc brakes, and Shimano groupset. As far as I understand, claris is the lower entry model.

My other concern is the size. I'm around 6' 3", and I measured my inside leg to be about 28". Do you think the 59cm frame size would be suitable?

Thanks.

It's got a freewheel hub. It's the sort of thing you'll find on a cheap department store bike. These are objectively inferior to freehubs and are incompatible with cassettes. If you want to upgrade, you'll have to replace the entire wheel. If you want matching rims, you'll have to replace both wheels. It's not a cheap upgrade.

It's a nice looking bike though.

The gearing is not so good for hill climbing. In my opinion, you'll want at least 10 speeds on an 11-32 cassette to allow you to spin your way up steep climbs without tiring yourself out. You'd need to replace the shifters as part of that upgrade, and STI shifters are very expensive. As mentioned previously, so are wheels, which would also be required as part of an upgrade to go from an 8 speed freewheel cog set to a 9, 10, or 11 speed cassette.

With regards to sizing, you should really go to a local bike shop and try a few frame sizes to get an idea of what size you need.
Thank you, this is exactly the sort of thing I wanted to know. I only know a little bit about bikes, I had to lookup the difference between freewheel hub and freehubs.

You're welcome. It may also interest you to know that I have come across several posts claiming there are additional safety concerns when dealing with 8 speed freewheels in particular. The axle of a freewheel is already at a greater risk of breaking due to the uneven stresses placed on it, but many people feel this risk is significantly higher with 8 speeds.
